reason: The text features several regular human characters who demonstrate agency throughout. Job is portrayed as a wealthy but ordinary person (not a king or prophet) who makes decisions about his household, performs religious rituals (sanctifying his children, offering burnt offerings), and responds intentionally to the disasters that befall him through acts of mourning and worship. His children actively gather for feasts and celebrations of their own volition. Servants and young men are depicted performing labor (plowing, herding animals). Even the messengers who arrive bear witness to human actors (the Sabeans and Chaldeans) taking deliberate military action. Throughout the narrative, human characters initiate actions, make choices, and respond to events, demonstrating meaningful agency despite the theological framework involving God and Satan that constrains or oversees these events.
